text: The backlog didn't fall steadily. It peaked at 4,593 in March 2025, then dropped to 2,924 in April and 2,145 in September 2025, when closures outpaced new requests (6,178 closed vs. 4,648 opened). It rose again to 3,505 by December 2025, and the output shows only 15 of 25 months, so the full trend is incomplete.
sql:
WITH av AS (
    SELECT created_at, closed_at
    FROM service_request
    WHERE sr_type ILIKE '%abandon%vehicle%'
      AND NOT is_canceled
      AND NOT is_duplicate
),
months AS (
    SELECT UNNEST(generate_series(
        (SELECT date_trunc('month', MIN(created_at)) FROM av),
        (SELECT date_trunc('month', MAX(created_at)) FROM av),
        INTERVAL 1 MONTH
    )) AS month_start
)
SELECT
    strftime(m.month_start, '%Y-%m') AS month,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM av a
      WHERE a.created_at >= m.month_start
        AND a.created_at < m.month_start + INTERVAL 1 MONTH) AS opened,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM av a
      WHERE a.closed_at >= m.month_start
        AND a.closed_at < m.month_start + INTERVAL 1 MONTH) AS closed,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM av a
      WHERE a.created_at < m.month_start + INTERVAL 1 MONTH
        AND (a.closed_at IS NULL OR a.closed_at >= m.month_start + INTERVAL 1 MONTH)) AS open_backlog
FROM months m
ORDER BY m.month_start

WITH cdot AS (
  SELECT sr.*
  FROM service_request sr
  JOIN department d ON sr.dept_code = d.dept_code

),
lighting AS (
  SELECT
    c.sr_type,
    c.community_area,
    c.created_at,
    c.closed_at,
    CASE WHEN c.sr_type ILIKE '%block%' THEN 'all-block' ELSE 'individual' END AS outage_scope

    AND NOT COALESCE(c.is_duplicate, FALSE)

    AND c.closed_at IS NOT NULL
),
timed AS (
  SELECT
    l.outage_scope,
    l.community_area,
    date_diff('day', l.created_at, l.closed_at) AS days_to_close,
    rb.benchmark_days
  FROM lighting l
  LEFT JOIN request_benchmark rb ON l.sr_type = rb.sr_type
)
SELECT
  t.outage_scope,
  ca.community_area_name,
  COUNT(*) AS request_count,
  median(t.days_to_close) AS median_days_to_close,
  ROUND(100.0 * AVG(CASE WHEN t.days_to_close <= t.benchmark_days THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 1) AS pct_within_benchmark

text: Citywide SLA attainment for service requests created in 2025 was 61.19%, measured across completed requests that were not canceled or flagged as duplicates.
sql:
WITH scoped AS (
    SELECT
        s.created_at,
        s.closed_at,
        b.benchmark_days
    FROM service_request s
    JOIN request_benchmark b
        ON s.sr_type = b.sr_type
    WHERE s.created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01'
      AND s.created_at <  TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
      AND s.closed_at IS NOT NULL
      AND COALESCE(s.is_canceled, FALSE) = FALSE
      AND COALESCE(s.is_duplicate, FALSE) = FALSE
)
SELECT
    ROUND(
        100.0 * AVG(
            CASE
                WHEN (epoch(closed_at) - epoch(created_at)) / 86400.0 <= benchmark_days
                THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0
            END
        ),
        2
    ) AS sla_attainment_pct
FROM scoped

text: In 2025, 40.4% of DWM's resolved requests (14,771 of 36,607) were closed on or before their benchmark, based on non-duplicate Completed requests with a positive benchmark.
sql:
WITH base AS (
    SELECT
        s.sr_number,
        b.benchmark_days,
        date_diff('second', s.created_at, s.closed_at) / 86400.0 AS elapsed_days
    FROM service_request s
    JOIN request_benchmark b
      ON lower(s.sr_type) = lower(b.sr_type)
    WHERE upper(s.dept_code) = 'DWM'
      AND s.created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01'
      AND s.created_at <  TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
      AND s.status = 'Completed'
      AND COALESCE(s.is_duplicate, FALSE) = FALSE
      AND s.closed_at IS NOT NULL
      AND b.benchmark_days > 0
)
SELECT
    CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN elapsed_days <= benchmark_days THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS DOUBLE)
        / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS on_time_fraction,
    SUM(CASE WHEN elapsed_days <= benchmark_days THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS on_time_count,
    COUNT(*) AS denominator
FROM base

text: CDOT completed 30.9% of its 29,539 eligible Q3 2026 requests within benchmark (9,119 on time), while DSS completed 29.9% of its 129,868 (38,870 on time). CDOT's on-time fraction is about one percentage point higher than DSS's.
sql:
WITH bm AS (
    SELECT lower(sr_type) AS sr_key,
           MAX(benchmark_days) AS benchmark_days
    FROM request_benchmark
    WHERE benchmark_days > 0
    GROUP BY lower(sr_type)
),
scoped AS (
    SELECT s.dept_code,
           s.created_at,
           s.closed_at,
           s.is_open,
           s.is_canceled,
           bm.benchmark_days
    FROM service_request s
    JOIN bm ON lower(s.sr_type) = bm.sr_key
    WHERE s.dept_code IN ('CDOT', 'DSS')
      AND COALESCE(s.is_duplicate, FALSE) = FALSE
      AND s.created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2026-07-01'
      AND s.created_at <  TIMESTAMP '2026-10-01'
)
SELECT dept_code,
       COUNT(*) AS denominator,
       SUM(CASE
             WHEN COALESCE(is_open, FALSE) = FALSE
              AND COALESCE(is_canceled, FALSE) = FALSE
              AND closed_at IS NOT NULL
              AND EXTRACT(epoch FROM (closed_at - created_at)) / 86400.0 <= benchmark_days
             THEN 1 ELSE 0
           END) AS on_time_count,
       CAST(SUM(CASE
             WHEN COALESCE(is_open, FALSE) = FALSE
              AND COALESCE(is_canceled, FALSE) = FALSE
              AND closed_at IS NOT NULL
              AND EXTRACT(epoch FROM (closed_at - created_at)) / 86400.0 <= benchmark_days
             THEN 1 ELSE 0
           END) AS DOUBLE) / COUNT(*) AS on_time_fraction
FROM scoped
GROUP BY dept_code

This may mean no CDOT requests matched the filters or the benchmark join dropped them, so it's worth checking the `request_benchmark` mapping for CDOT request types before relying on this figure.
sql:
WITH cdot AS (
    SELECT
        sr.sr_number,
        sr.created_at,
        sr.closed_at,
        sr.is_open,
        sr.is_canceled,
        b.benchmark_days,
        CASE
            WHEN COALESCE(sr.is_open, FALSE) = FALSE
             AND COALESCE(sr.is_canceled, FALSE) = FALSE
             AND sr.closed_at IS NOT NULL
             AND (epoch(sr.closed_at) - epoch(sr.created_at)) / 86400.0 <= b.benchmark_days
            THEN 1 ELSE 0
        END AS is_success
    FROM service_request sr
    JOIN request_benchmark b
      ON b.sr_type = sr.sr_type
    WHERE sr.dept_code = 'CDOT'
      AND sr.created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2026-04-01'
      AND sr.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-07-01'
      AND COALESCE(sr.is_duplicate, FALSE) = FALSE
      AND b.benchmark_days > 0
)
SELECT
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(is_success) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 2) AS pct_within_benchmark,
    COUNT(*) AS denominator,
    SUM(is_success) AS successful_count
FROM cdot
